diagrams.title: Controls Matrix: Which Control for Which Layer?
diagrams.subtitle: Each cell gives a control and its intended effect. Click cells to compare detection, prevention, and response.

cells.detail: NIDS analyzes a copy of traffic out-of-band; WIPS monitors for rogue wireless access points. Neither blocks by itself.
HIDS alerts on file changes; EDR detects behaviors on the agent; XDR correlates multiple sources.
Detects hardcoded keys and passwords in code and repository history. Exam objective control, absent from the books.
DMARC reports reveal senders spoofing the domain and messages failing alignment.
NIPS blocks inline, WAF filters HTTP at the application layer, 802.1X denies access before authentication.
HIPS blocks locally, MDM enforces mobile policy, SELinux applies mandatory access control.
Validating inputs prevents injection; signing code guarantees origin and integrity of binaries.
SPF lists authorized servers, DKIM signs the message, DMARC rejects or quarantines alignment failures.
Limits request abuse and reduces the impact of a flood without waiting for full analysis.
EDR isolates a compromised host from the network; quarantine blocks a suspicious file detected by antivirus.
DLP blocks copying or sending sensitive data; rollback restores a known-good state.
BIMI displays the verified logo and DMARC with a reject policy blocks domain spoofing.
Entire network of decoys: reveals reconnaissance and lateral movement in the simulated zone.
Decoy account or token: any use is a high-confidence signal.
Bait file whose opening or copying betrays unauthorized access.
A monitored decoy email address reveals address-harvesting campaigns.
